selected.title: Trump strikes deal with Putin for Russia to supply diesel to US
selected.summary: In an apparent reversal of Washington's campaign to squeeze Russian fuel revenue powering the war in Ukraine, Donald Trump says Moscow will supply diesel to the US.
selected.why: Major sanctions and trade policy reversal with significant implications for global energy markets.
selected.fullText: Energy minister Chris Bowen rejects Trump-Putin diesel supply plan - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home More Ukraine-Russia news Share Share article Energy minister Chris Bowen rejects Trump-Putin diesel supply plan Topic: Oil and Gas Posted Sat 10 Oct 2026 at 9:43am Sat 10 Oct 2026 at 9:43am Sat 10 Oct 2026 at 9:43am Donald Trump (right) says he had a "highly successful" phone call with Vladimir Putin over diesel supply. ( Reuters: Kevin Lamarque ) In short: Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply diesel to the US. Mr Trump signed sweeping sanctions against Russia last month aimed at clamping down on Russia's energy revenues. Analysts have cast doubt on how much the deal will ease near record-high diesel prices in the US. abc.net.au/news/trump-strikes-deal-with-putin-for-russia-to-supply-diesel-to-us/107250922 Link copied Share Share article US President Donald Trump says he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, up-ending years of Washington pressuring Moscow over its war with Ukraine. The price of diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, sits near a record high in the US. Mr Trump said on social media he had a "highly successful" discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin in which they agreed Moscow would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets. Energy minister Chris Bowen told Weekend Breakfast that Australia "doesn't need or want Russian fuel". "We have the arrangements in place as best as we possibly can with our trading partners to ensure that Russian fuel doesn't flow to Australia," he said. "We do not want Vladimir Putin to benefit from this war in the Middle East." Mr Bowen stopped short of condemning the United States but reiterated Australia was firmly against Russia being rewarded "for their illegal and immoral invasion of Ukraine by any arrangements put in place". Analyst warns diesel prices could top $4 a litre Analyst warns export ban the most worrying development since the Middle East conflict began. An envoy for Mr Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, praised the cooperation between Russia and the US in a post on X shortly after the call. Only last month Mr Trump signed a sweeping sanctions law aimed at clamping down on Russia’s energy revenues and other areas that are fuelling its war against Ukraine.
